title: Profile and optimize vector429 Round2
objective: Profile vector429 p=2 through the shared native Round2 resource and materially reduce its dominant general kernel or route it through a bounded exact selector without fixture-specific logic

oracles: ordinary Python Round2 exact local HNF
forced original exact native multiplier and basis transformations
exceptions: Bounded optimization of the existing audited FLINT/GMP Round2 representation primitive; no new mathematical algorithm

handoff.summary: The second pass applies the exact Round-2 block form [I R; 0 pI] directly to the multiplication tensor, retaining unchanged generators and restricting p-squared division to the pivot block. Combined results reduce vector429 p=2 from 19.398s to 6.129s and vector010 p=2 from 0.906s to 0.233s. Both high-degree payloads match the forced generic implementation byte-for-byte; focused randomized and sanitizer checks pass.
risks: The block transform still accounts for 70.2% of vector429 and 48.9% of vector010 Round-2 time; reaching vector010's 74ms target now also requires reducing its 69ms multiplier, 33ms modular-table, and 14ms radical phases.
The audited header metrics are intentionally not edited in this distribution lane, so central integration must refresh architecture/native-audit.json before architecture:check.
next_steps: Update the number_field_order_ffi.h audit metrics from 1410 lines/58164 bytes to 1639 lines/68585 bytes and extend its existing exact block-transform rationale, then run pnpm architecture:check.
Retain the current generic native-first word-prime selector: vector010 p=2 native is 113.7x faster than forced Round-4 while forced polygon and OM each exceed 30 seconds.
Run the full native/platform validation suite from the integration lane; Windows continues to use the exact tested fallback where the optimized host capability is unavailable.
